problem:
Consider the matrices given below. Find $\,\text{dim(Null}(A))+\text{dim(Null}(B))+\text{dim(Null}(C)).$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 7 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & -5 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

activity_context.topic_title: The Dimension of the Null Space of a Matrix

feedback.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

- If $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 5 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(A))=2.$
- If $B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(B))=3.$
- If $C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(C))=2.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The dimension of the null space of a matrix is the number of non-pivot columns in the matrix. 

Also, all of the given matrices are in row echelon form.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the statements.

- Statement I is true. The matrix $A$ has $3$ pivot columns and $2$ non-pivot columns. So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))=2.
$$

- Statement II is false. The matrix $B$ has $3$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $4$th column). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(B))=1.
$$

- Statement III is false. The matrix $C$ has $2$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $2$nd column). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(C))=1.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
